newsitem.title: USA: FTC tips on leasing a car.
newsitem.headline: FTC tips on leasing a car.

text.p: If you're thinking of leasing a car, the Federal Trade Commission offers these tips:
1. Shop as if you're buying a car. Negotiate all the terms, including price, and get them in writing.

2. Ask about extra charges. Most leases let you drive 12,000 to 15,000 miles a year but charge 10 to 25 cents for each extra mile. You may think a dent is covered under normal "wear and tear," when the dealer considers it major damage.
3. Check out penalties for returning the car early; expect charges to be steep.
4. Make sure the manufacturer's warranty covers the entire lease term and the number of miles you're likely to drive.
5. Consider "gap insurance" to cover the difference between what you owe on the lease and what it's worth if it's stolen or wrecked in an accident.
--In a closed-end lease, you're usually responsible for certain end-of-lease charges, such as excess mileage.
--In an open-end lease, you pay the difference between the value stated in your contract and the lessor's appraised value at the end of the lease.
--Lease inception fees are payments made when lease starts and may include down payment, security deposit and first month's payment. Ask for a list; you may be able to negotiate.
--The capitalised cost is the price of the car for leasing purposes plus taxes and extra charges like registration fees.

--The capitalised cost reduction is similar to a down payment. If you're trading in a car, be sure the dealer applies the trade-in value to the price your lease is based on. The credit may reduce your payments.
